summary: Flathead County, MT tower on Lion Hill near Hungry Horse: 50-ft pole L-4 tower from 1932, destroyed 1950; no source describes what remains today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1950 according to firelookout.com; no source describes the site now

events.note: 50-foot pole L-4 tower listed for 1932 on firelookout.com
firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1950'; the page gives no cause

evidence.supports: Lion Hill is in Flathead County, Montana
the lookout is about three miles southeast of Hungry Horse
the lookout is on the Flathead National Forest
a 50-foot pole L-4 tower stood from 1932
the Forest Fire Lookout Association list records the Lion Hill tower as gone, at 48.35663, -114.01433
a proposed Forest Service fuel break would run along Lion Hill Road (Forest Service Road No. 5311)
evidence.quote: the Lion Hill fuel break would be located along Lion Hill Road (Forest Service Road No. 5311)

evidence.supports: the fuel break location is just south of Martin City (article is about a proposal, not the lookout site)

sources.title: Forest Service plans fuel breaks for Lion Hill, East Side Road

notes_for_editor: The destruction date (1950) rests on one page, firelookout.com; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list agrees only on 'Gone' and gives no date. The brief's record (tower, gone, Flathead County) holds, so no corrections. Staffing and fires are left out because no source covers them. Kemnow's Forest Lookouts page gives only a legal location (30N-19W-15) and no history. The 2023 Hungry Horse News item is about a proposed fuel break and does not describe the lookout site. Access level is omitted because no source gives it. Search budget: two websearch.py queries and about six page reads for this tower.
